name: M3-Embedding: Multi-Linguality, Multi-Functionality, Multi-Granularity Text Embeddings
problem: Retrieval systems needed a separate model per retrieval style, language and input length.
mechanism: One dense model supporting THREE retrieval functions simultaneously - dense, MULTI-VECTOR (late interaction) and SPARSE (lexical) - over 100+ languages and inputs from short sentences to 8192-token documents. Trained with self-knowledge distillation, where relevance scores from the different retrieval functions are combined into a teacher signal for each other.
speedup_reported: Reports new state-of-the-art on multilingual, cross-lingual and long-document retrieval benchmarks. No latency, throughput or hardware figures are given, so there is no serving-cost claim to extract.
notes: SLUG RENAMED 2026-10-04 (parent agent): was 'bge-m3', colliding with the models record of the same id, which made every bare-slug cross-reference ambiguous. Inbound refs ([]) all mean the models record, so none needed repointing; papers are cited via `sources`, never by bare slug. Venue ACL Findings 2024 (crossref 'Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics'). THE SERVING-RELEVANT PART IS THE THREE-FUNCTION SUPPORT, and it cuts against the single-vector orthodoxy: this one checkpoint can emit a dense vector for ANN search, a sparse vector for inverted-index retrieval, and multi-vector ColBERT-style vectors for reranking. That collapses three separate model deployments into one, and the sparse head in particular is the cheapest of the three at query time. The multi-vector head carries the ColBERT memory cost documented in pap-mm-colbert.
